claim: In substance use disorders, drug use as unconditioned stimulus (US) reinforces drug taking.
source: In substance use disorders, drug use as unconditioned stimulus (US) reinforces drug taking.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that draws on established scientific understanding of substance use disorders.

claim: Drug-associated cues (conditioned stimulus [CS]) gain incentive salience to promote drug seeking.
source: Meanwhile, drug-associated cues (conditioned stimulus [CS]) also gain incentive salience to promote drug seeking.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that draws on established scientific understanding of conditioned responses in substance use.

claim: The basolateral amygdala (BLA) is implicated in both US- and CS-mediated responses.
source: The basolateral amygdala (BLA) is implicated in both US- and CS-mediated responses.
evidence: This statement draws on established scientific knowledge about the BLA's role in reward processing.

claim: Two genetically distinct BLA neuronal types express Rspo2 versus Ppp1r1b, respectively.
source: Here, we show that two genetically distinct BLA neuronal types, expressing Rspo2 versus Ppp1r1b, respectively, project to the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and form monosynaptic connections with both dopamine D1 and D2 receptor-expressing neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript, including viral tracing and electrophysiology.

claim: Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons project to the nucleus accumbens (NAc).
source: Here, we show that two genetically distinct BLA neuronal types, expressing Rspo2 versus Ppp1r1b, respectively, project to the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and form monosynaptic connections with both dopamine D1 and D2 receptor-expressing neurons.
evidence: This is supported by viral tracing experiments shown in Figure 1 and electrophysiological recordings.

claim: Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons form monosynaptic connections with both dopamine D1 and D2 receptor-expressing neurons in the NAc.
source: Here, we show that two genetically distinct BLA neuronal types, expressing Rspo2 versus Ppp1r1b, respectively, project to the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and form monosynaptic connections with both dopamine D1 and D2 receptor-expressing neurons.
evidence: This is demonstrated by optogenetic stimulation and electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1K-L and 1W-X.

claim: Intra-NAc stimulation of Rspo2 presynaptic terminals establishes intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS).
source: While intra-NAc stimulation of Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b presynaptic terminals establishes intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS), only Ppp1r1b-stimulated mice exhibit cue-induced ICSS seeking.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Intra-NAc stimulation of Ppp1r1b presynaptic terminals establishes intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS).
source: While intra-NAc stimulation of Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b presynaptic terminals establishes intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS), only Ppp1r1b-stimulated mice exhibit cue-induced ICSS seeking.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Only Ppp1r1b-stimulated mice exhibit cue-induced ICSS seeking.
source: While intra-NAc stimulation of Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b presynaptic terminals establishes intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS), only Ppp1r1b-stimulated mice exhibit cue-induced ICSS seeking.
evidence: This is supported by extinction test data shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: Increasing the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection increases cue-induced cocaine seeking after cocaine withdrawal.
source: Furthermore, increasing versus decreasing the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc, but not Rspo2-to-NAc, subprojection increases versus decreases cue-induced cocaine seeking after cocaine withdrawal.
evidence: This is supported by chemogenetic manipulation data shown in Figure 4X.

claim: Decreasing the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection decreases cue-induced cocaine seeking after cocaine withdrawal.
source: Furthermore, increasing versus decreasing the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc, but not Rspo2-to-NAc, subprojection increases versus decreases cue-induced cocaine seeking after cocaine withdrawal.
evidence: This is supported by chemogenetic manipulation data shown in Figure 4R.

claim: Manipulating the Rspo2-to-NAc subprojection does not affect cue-induced cocaine seeking after cocaine withdrawal.
source: Furthermore, increasing versus decreasing the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc, but not Rspo2-to-NAc, subprojection increases versus decreases cue-induced cocaine seeking after cocaine withdrawal.
evidence: This is supported by chemogenetic manipulation data shown in Figure 4O and 4U.

claim: Both BLA-to-NAc subprojections contribute to US-mediated responses.
source: Thus, while both BLA-to-NAc subprojections contribute to US-mediated responses, the Ppp1r1b subprojection selectively encodes CS-mediated reward and drug reinforcement.
evidence: This is inferred from the ICSS data showing both subprojections can establish self-stimulation.

claim: The Ppp1r1b subprojection selectively encodes CS-mediated reward and drug reinforcement.
source: Thus, while both BLA-to-NAc subprojections contribute to US-mediated responses, the Ppp1r1b subprojection selectively encodes CS-mediated reward and drug reinforcement.
evidence: This is supported by the cue-induced ICSS seeking and cocaine seeking data.

claim: During the development of substance use disorder, the drug as an unconditioned stimulus (US) with its primary rewarding effects drives drug taking and seeking.
source: During the development of substance use disorder, the drug as an unconditioned stimulus (US) with its primary rewarding effects drives drug taking and seeking (Venniro et al., 2020; Nader, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Drug-associated environmental cues acquire incentive salience to promote drug seeking and relapse.
source: Meanwhile, drug use is often associated with conditioned stimuli (CS), such as environmental cues, which also acquire incentive salience to promote drug seeking and relapse (Venniro et al., 2020; Nader, 2016; Volkow et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The nucleus accumbens (NAc) is a key brain region where medium spiny neurons (MSNs) process both US and CS inputs for behavioral outputs.
source: The nucleus accumbens (NAc) is a key brain region where medium spiny neurons (MSNs) process both US and CS inputs for behavioral outputs (Meredith et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The basolateral amygdala (BLA) provides both US- and CS-associated input to the NAc during drug taking and seeking.
source: Using region-specific lesion, pharmacological inhibition, and optogenetic manipulation, extensive previous studies demonstrate that the basolateral amygdala (BLA) provides both US- and CS-associated input to the NAc during drug taking and seeking (Cardinal et al., 2002; Wright and Dong, 2020; Zinsmaier et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies using various experimental approaches.

claim: BLA pyramidal neurons heterogeneously respond to US, CS, as well as stimuli with appetitive or aversive valence.
source: BLA pyramidal neurons heterogeneously respond to US, CS, as well as stimuli with appetitive or aversive valence (Janak and Tye, 2015; O'Neill et al., 2018; Gründemann et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLA neurons are genetically separable into two populations: R-spondin2-positive (Rspo2) magnocellular neurons and protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B-positive (Ppp1r1b) parvocellular neurons.
source: These BLA neurons are genetically separable into two populations, R-spondin2-positive (Rspo2) magnocellular neurons and protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B-positive (Ppp1r1b, also known as DARPP-32) parvocellular neurons (Kim et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies that characterized these neuronal populations.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of ChR2-expressing Rspo2 axon fibers evokes excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) in both D1 and D2 MSNs.
source: In both D1 and D2 MSNs, such stimulations evoked fast-activating and fast-decaying synaptic responses that were inhibited by the antagonists of glutamatergic receptors (NBQX 10 μM, D-AP5 50 μM), indicating that these synaptic responses were excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) mediated by Rspo2-to-NAc monosynaptic transmission (Figure 1K, L).
evidence: This is demonstrated by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1K-L.

claim: EPSCs evoked by Rspo2-to-NAc stimulation are mediated by glutamatergic receptors.
source: In both D1 and D2 MSNs, such stimulations evoked fast-activating and fast-decaying synaptic responses that were inhibited by the antagonists of glutamatergic receptors (NBQX 10 μM, D-AP5 50 μM), indicating that these synaptic responses were excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) mediated by Rspo2-to-NAc monosynaptic transmission (Figure 1K, L).
evidence: This is demonstrated by pharmacological blockade experiments shown in Figure 1K-L.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of ChR2-expressing Ppp1r1b axon fibers evokes EPSCs in both D1 and D2 NAc MSNs.
source: Optogenetic stimulation of these Ppp1r1b fibers evoked EPSCs in both D1 and D2 NAc MSNs (Figure 1V–X).
evidence: This is demonstrated by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1V-X.

claim: Both Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons project to the NAc and form monosynaptic connections with both D1 and D2 MSNs.
source: Thus, both Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons project to the NAc and form monosynaptic connections with both D1 and D2 MSNs.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the electrophysiological data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The paired-pulse ratio (PPR) is inversely correlated with the presynaptic release probability (Pr).
source: The paired-pulse ratio (PPR), which is inversely correlated with the presynaptic release probability (Pr), was generally lower at Ppp1r1b synapses than Rspo2 synapses, suggesting a higher basal Pr at Ppp1r1b synapses (Figure 1Z).
evidence: This is established knowledge in synaptic physiology.

claim: PPR is generally lower at Ppp1r1b synapses than Rspo2 synapses.
source: The paired-pulse ratio (PPR), which is inversely correlated with the presynaptic release probability (Pr), was generally lower at Ppp1r1b synapses than Rspo2 synapses, suggesting a higher basal Pr at Ppp1r1b synapses (Figure 1Z).
evidence: This is demonstrated by paired-pulse stimulation experiments shown in Figure 1Y-Z.

claim: Ppp1r1b synapses have a higher basal presynaptic release probability than Rspo2 synapses.
source: The paired-pulse ratio (PPR), which is inversely correlated with the presynaptic release probability (Pr), was generally lower at Ppp1r1b synapses than Rspo2 synapses, suggesting a higher basal Pr at Ppp1r1b synapses (Figure 1Z).
evidence: This is inferred from the PPR data shown in Figure 1Z.

claim: For either Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmissions, EPSCs recorded in D1 and D2 MSNs exhibited similar PPRs.
source: Furthermore, for either Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmissions, EPSCs recorded in D1 and D2 MSNs exhibited similar PPRs, suggesting that each subprojection synapses on D1 and D2 MSNs with a similar Pr (Figure 1Z).
evidence: This is demonstrated by PPR data shown in Figure 1Z.

claim: Each BLA subprojection synapses on D1 and D2 MSNs with a similar presynaptic release probability.
source: Furthermore, for either Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmissions, EPSCs recorded in D1 and D2 MSNs exhibited similar PPRs, suggesting that each subprojection synapses on D1 and D2 MSNs with a similar Pr (Figure 1Z).
evidence: This is inferred from the PPR data shown in Figure 1Z.

claim: Both Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b subprojections form functional glutamatergic synapses on both NAc shell and core MSNs.
source: For each of the subprojections, we recorded reliable EPSCs in MSNs from both the NAc shell and core, indicating that both Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b subprojections form functional glutamatergic synapses on both NAc shell and core MSNs.
evidence: This is based on electrophysiological recordings from both NAc subregions.

claim: The Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b subprojections formed monosynaptic synapses with NAc MSNs, with presynaptic properties exhibiting between-projection difference.
source: Taken together, the Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b subprojections formed monosynaptic synapses with NAc MSNs, with presynaptic properties exhibiting between-projection difference.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the electrophysiological data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Intra-NAc laser stimulation at 20 or 40 Hz did not establish ICSS in control mice expressing YFP in BLA Rspo2-to-NAc terminals.
source: In control mice in which Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b neurons expressed YFP alone without ChR2, intra-NAc laser stimulation at either 20 or 40 Hz did not induce ICSS (Figure 2BC).
evidence: This is demonstrated by behavioral data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Intra-NAc laser stimulation at 20 or 40 Hz did not establish ICSS in control mice expressing YFP in BLA Ppp1r1b-to-NAc terminals.
source: In control mice in which Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b neurons expressed YFP alone without ChR2, intra-NAc laser stimulation at either 20 or 40 Hz did not induce ICSS (Figure 2BC).
evidence: This is demonstrated by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In Rspo2-ChR2 mice, stimulations at 40 Hz, but not 20 Hz, established ICSS.
source: In Rspo2-ChR2 or Ppp1r1b-ChR2 mice, stimulations at 40 Hz, but not 20 Hz or lower (data not shown), established ICSS (Figure 2DE).
evidence: This is demonstrated by behavioral data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In Ppp1r1b-ChR2 mice, stimulations at 40 Hz, but not 20 Hz, established ICSS.
source: In Rspo2-ChR2 or Ppp1r1b-ChR2 mice, stimulations at 40 Hz, but not 20 Hz or lower (data not shown), established ICSS (Figure 2DE).
evidence: This is demonstrated by behavioral data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Strong, but not moderate, activation of the axonal fibers of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection reinforces operant responding.
source: Thus, strong, but not moderate, activation of the axonal fibers of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection reinforces operant responding.
evidence: This is inferred from the frequency-dependent ICSS establishment data.

claim: Rspo2-ChR2 mice decreased their operant response to the level of Rspo2-YFP control mice over 3 days of extinction testing.
source: Over 3 days of such testing, Rspo2-ChR2 mice decreased their operant response to the level as in Rspo2-YFP control mice (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by extinction test data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Ppp1r1b-ChR2 mice maintained high levels of responses to the active lever throughout the 3-day extinction testing.
source: In contrast, Ppp1r1b-ChR2 mice maintained high levels of responses to the active lever throughout the 3-day testing (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by extinction test data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Activation of Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection may assign incentive salience to conditioned cues.
source: Thus, in addition to inducing ICSS, activation of Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection may also assign incentive salience to conditioned cues, providing a circuit-based encoding for CS-mediated operant responses in the absence of US.
evidence: This is inferred from the persistent cue-induced responding in Ppp1r1b-ChR2 mice during extinction.

claim: Ppp1r1b-ChR2, but not Rspo2-ChR2, mice exhibited persistent cue-induced lever pressing after 21 days of abstinence.
source: Ppp1r1b-ChR2, but not Rspo2-ChR2, mice exhibited persistent cue-induced lever pressing, indicating the durable feature of the CS-mediated reinforcement established through the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection (Figure 2HI).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cue-induced seeking test data shown in Figure 2H-I.

claim: The CS-mediated reinforcement established through the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection has a durable feature.
source: Ppp1r1b-ChR2, but not Rspo2-ChR2, mice exhibited persistent cue-induced lever pressing, indicating the durable feature of the CS-mediated reinforcement established through the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection (Figure 2HI).
evidence: This is inferred from the persistent cue-induced responding after 21 days of abstinence.

claim: Stimulation of either the Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection may serve as a US for establishing ICSS.
source: Despite ICSS-related caveats (see Discussion), the above results indicate that stimulation of either the Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection may serve as a US for establishing ICSS, while the Ppp1r1b subprojection functions as a key component within the BLA-to-NAc input that encodes CS-mediated reinforcement.
evidence: This is inferred from the ICSS establishment data.

claim: The Ppp1r1b subprojection functions as a key component within the BLA-to-NAc input that encodes CS-mediated reinforcement.
source: Despite ICSS-related caveats (see Discussion), the above results indicate that stimulation of either the Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection may serve as a US for establishing ICSS, while the Ppp1r1b subprojection functions as a key component within the BLA-to-NAc input that encodes CS-mediated reinforcement.
evidence: This is inferred from the cue-induced ICSS seeking data.

claim: The BLA-to-NAc projection is one of the primary circuit underpinnings for cue-conditioned cocaine seeking.
source: The BLA-to-NAc projection is one of the primary circuit underpinnings for cue-conditioned cocaine seeking (Wright and Dong, 2020; Zinsmaier et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activation of SSFO upon 473 nm laser stimulation generates a low but persistent conductance to cations.
source: Activation of SSFO upon 473 nm laser stimulation generates a low but persistent (deactivation tau at ~29 min) conductance to cations (Yizhar et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature describing SSFO properties.

claim: Activation of SSFO does not evoke action potentials but instead moderately depolarizes the membrane potential to facilitate presynaptic release.
source: With these features, activation of SSFO does not evoke action potentials but instead moderately depolarizes the membrane potential to facilitate presynaptic release (Yizhar et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature and is consistent with established knowledge about SSFO function.

claim: Laser stimulation (473 nm, 50 ms × 10 pulses at 10 Hz) turns on SSFO, which persistently (>40 min) and selectively facilitates presynaptic release from BLA projections to NAc MSNs without generating back-propagating action potentials.
source: After viral-mediated expression of SSFO in the prefrontal cortex or BLA, our previous studies verify that laser stimulation (473 nm, 50 ms × 10 pulses at 10 Hz) turns on SSFO, which persistently (>40 min) and selectively facilitates presynaptic release from these projections to NAc MSNs without generating back-propagating action potentials (Wang et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies by the authors.

claim: A 473 nm laser train (10 pulses at 10 Hz) of stimulation increased the frequency without affecting the amplitude of sEPSCs in NAc MSNs.
source: A 473 nm laser train (10 pulses at 10 Hz) of stimulation increased the frequency (F2,10 = 6.0, p=0.02) without affecting the amplitude (F2,10 = 1.3, p=0.33) of sEPSCs, and this effect of SSFO was terminated upon application of a 590 nm laser train (10 pulses at 10 Hz), indicating an effective and reversible presynaptic upregulation by SSFO (Figure 3CD).
evidence: This is demonstrated by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: The effect of SSFO on sEPSC frequency was terminated upon application of a 590 nm laser train.
source: A 473 nm laser train (10 pulses at 10 Hz) of stimulation increased the frequency (F2,10 = 6.0, p=0.02) without affecting the amplitude (F2,10 = 1.3, p=0.33) of sEPSCs, and this effect of SSFO was terminated upon application of a 590 nm laser train (10 pulses at 10 Hz), indicating an effective and reversible presynaptic upregulation by SSFO (Figure 3CD).
evidence: This is demonstrated by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: SSFO provides an effective and reversible presynaptic upregulation.
source: A 473 nm laser train (10 pulses at 10 Hz) of stimulation increased the frequency (F2,10 = 6.0, p=0.02) without affecting the amplitude (F2,10 = 1.3, p=0.33) of sEPSCs, and this effect of SSFO was terminated upon application of a 590 nm laser train (10 pulses at 10 Hz), indicating an effective and reversible presynaptic upregulation by SSFO (Figure 3CD).
evidence: This is inferred from the reversible effect on sEPSC frequency shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: Upregulation of Rspo2-to-NAc transmission does not affect the performance of cocaine SA.
source: With this manipulation, neither the response to active lever nor cocaine intake was altered in Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b mice on day 6, compared to the day before or after (Figure 3F, G). Thus, upregulation of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmission does not affect the performance of cocaine SA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine SA data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Upregulation of Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmission does not affect the performance of cocaine SA.
source: With this manipulation, neither the response to active lever nor cocaine intake was altered in Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b mice on day 6, compared to the day before or after (Figure 3F, G). Thus, upregulation of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmission does not affect the performance of cocaine SA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine SA data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Downregulation of Rspo2-to-NAc transmission does not affect the acquisition or performance of cocaine SA.
source: Over 10 days of cocaine SA, both Rspo2-CNO and Ppp1r1b-CNO mice exhibited similar levels of active lever responding and cocaine intake compared to control mice, which expressed DREADDs but with daily intra-NAc infusion of 500 nL of saline (Figure 3K–N). Thus, downregulation of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmission does not affect the acquisition or performance of cocaine SA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine SA data shown in Figure 3K-L.

claim: Downregulation of Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmission does not affect the acquisition or performance of cocaine SA.
source: Over 10 days of cocaine SA, both Rspo2-CNO and Ppp1r1b-CNO mice exhibited similar levels of active lever responding and cocaine intake compared to control mice, which expressed DREADDs but with daily intra-NAc infusion of 500 nL of saline (Figure 3K–N). Thus, downregulation of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmission does not affect the acquisition or performance of cocaine SA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine SA data shown in Figure 3M-N.

claim: Neither the Rspo2- nor Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection is essential for acquiring and maintaining the operant response for cocaine.
source: Taken together, neither the Rspo2- nor Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojection seems to be essential for acquiring and maintaining the operant response for cocaine, leading our subsequent experiments to explore the role of these subprojections in cue-conditioned responses after cocaine SA was established.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of effect of manipulating these subprojections on cocaine SA.

claim: Through cocaine SA, conditioned cues acquire reinforcing properties that drive cocaine seeking.
source: Through cocaine SA, conditioned cues acquire reinforcing properties that drive cocaine seeking.
evidence: This is established knowledge in addiction neuroscience.

claim: Cue-induced cocaine seeking was not altered in Rspo2-hM4D mice upon intra-NAc application of CNO.
source: Rspo2 mice with hM4D-CNO exhibited similar levels of cue-induced cocaine seeking compared to the hM4D-saline control mice (Figure 4O).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine seeking test data shown in Figure 4O.

claim: Cue-induced cocaine seeking was decreased in Ppp1r1b mice with hM4D-CNO, compared to hM4D-saline controls.
source: However, cue-induced cocaine seeking was decreased in Ppp1r1b mice with hM4D-CNO, compared to hM4D-saline controls (Figure 4R).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine seeking test data shown in Figure 4R.

claim: hM3D-CNO and hM3D-saline Rspo2 mice exhibited similar levels of cue-induced cocaine seeking.
source: While hM3D-CNO and hM3D-saline Rspo2 mice exhibited similar levels of cue-induced cocaine seeking (Figure 4U), cue-induced cocaine seeking was increased in hM3D-CNO Ppp1r1b mice (Figure 4X).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine seeking test data shown in Figure 4U.

claim: Cue-induced cocaine seeking was increased in hM3D-CNO Ppp1r1b mice.
source: While hM3D-CNO and hM3D-saline Rspo2 mice exhibited similar levels of cue-induced cocaine seeking (Figure 4U), cue-induced cocaine seeking was increased in hM3D-CNO Ppp1r1b mice (Figure 4X).
evidence: This is demonstrated by cocaine seeking test data shown in Figure 4X.

claim: The Ppp1r1b subprojection is a key component of the BLA-to-NAc circuit that regulates the behavioral expression of cue-conditioned cocaine seeking.
source: These results suggest the Ppp1r1b subprojection as a key component of the BLA-to-NAc circuit that regulates the behavioral expression of cue-conditioned cocaine seeking.
evidence: This is inferred from the bidirectional chemogenetic manipulation effects on cue-induced cocaine seeking.

claim: The two BLA-to-NAc subprojections may be part of the circuit mechanism through which US- and CS-mediated reinforcements are differentially encoded.
source: The two BLA-to-NAc subprojections may be part of the circuit mechanism through which US- and CS-mediated reinforcements are differentially encoded and, thus, can be targeted for selective manipulation of drug- versus cue-induced drug relapse.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: The BLA projection to NAc is critically implicated in both US- and CS-mediated reinforcement, including drug- and cue-induced drug seeking.
source: The BLA projection to NAc is critically implicated in both US- and CS-mediated reinforcement, including drug- and cue-induced drug seeking (Everitt and Robbins, 2005; Puaud et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In behaving animals, BLA neurons tend to be activated in a population-specific manner in response to US versus CS as well as stimuli with different valences.
source: In behaving animals, BLA neurons tend to be activated in a population-specific manner in response to US versus CS as well as stimuli with different valences, suggesting the functional and populational heterogeneity of BLA neurons (O'Neill et al., 2018; Paton et al., 2006; Tye and Janak, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BLA pyramidal neurons can be divided into two populations: magnocellular versus parvocellular neurons that are preferentially located in the anterior versus posterior BLA, respectively.
source: Based on morphological and anatomical properties, BLA pyramidal neurons can be divided into two populations, magnocellular versus parvocellular neurons that are preferentially located in the anterior versus posterior BLA, respectively (Swanson and Petrovich, 1998; McDonald, 1982).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Magnocellular and parvocellular BLA neurons correspond to Rspo2- and Ppp1r1b-expressing neurons, which are differentially implicated in appetitive versus aversive affective responding.
source: Genetic profiling reveals that these two neuronal types correspond to Rspo2- and Ppp1r1b-expressing neurons, which are differentially implicated in appetitive versus aversive affective responding (Kim et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Stimulation of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc presynaptic fibers evokes EPSCs in randomly sampled MSNs, suggesting co-innervation of individual MSNs by both BLA subprojections.
source: In our experiments, stimulation of Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc presynaptic fibers evokes EPSCs in randomly sampled MSNs, suggesting co-innervation of individual MSNs by both BLA subprojections.
evidence: This is inferred from the electrophysiological recording data.

claim: If co-innervation is true, each MSN may function as a basic NAc unit to integrate Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b inputs.
source: Nonetheless, if co-innervation is true, each MSN may function as a basic NAc unit to integrate Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b inputs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the co-innervation hypothesis.

claim: D1 and D2 NAc MSNs play differential and, on many occasions, opposing roles in cue-conditioned responses.
source: Potentially through different downstream targets, D1 and D2 NAc MSNs play differential and, on many occasions, opposing roles in cue-conditioned responses (Zinsmaier et al., 2022; Smith et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The co-innervation of D1 and D2 MSNs by Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b provides a circuit basis on which the dynamic balance between the drive and inhibition can be achieved.
source: We speculate that the co-innervation of D1 and D2 MSNs by Rspo2 or Ppp1r1b provides a circuit basis on which the dynamic balance between the drive and inhibition can be achieved.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the co-innervation pattern and known functions of D1 and D2 MSNs.

claim: The presynaptic Pr of Ppp1r1b synapses is higher than Rspo2 synapses.
source: Because both subprojections are assessed by stimulation of ChR2-expressing presynaptic terminals with the same set of parameters, potential systemic errors are normalized. These results suggest that the presynaptic Pr of Ppp1r1b synapses is higher than Rspo2 synapses.
evidence: This is inferred from the PPR data showing lower PPR at Ppp1r1b synapses.

claim: In response to CS, BLA neurons fire action potentials with heterogenous patterns.
source: In response to CS, BLA neurons fire action potentials with heterogenous patterns (Ambroggi et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The Rspo2- versus Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmissions are expected to be more effective in activating NAc MSNs upon bursting versus tonic activations, respectively.
source: With these synaptic features, the Rspo2- versus Ppp1r1b-to-NAc transmissions are expected to be more effective in activating NAc MSNs upon bursting versus tonic activations, respectively.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the different PPRs of the two subprojections.

claim: Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons may encode opposite valence such that they selectively express activity biomarkers in response to aversive versus appetitive stimuli, respectively.
source: However, recent results show that Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons may encode opposite valence such that they selectively express activity biomarkers in response to aversive versus appetitive stimuli, respectively (Kim et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Compared with the NAc, a larger portion of Rspo2 neurons send much denser projections to the central nucleus of amygdala (CeA).
source: Specifically, results from the retrograde tracing show that, compared with the NAc, a larger portion of Rspo2 neurons send much denser projections to the central nucleus of amygdala (CeA), a brain region associated with negative behaviors (Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: BLA neurons that project to the CeA versus NAc are preferentially activated by aversion- versus reward-predictive cues.
source: BLA neurons that project to the CeA versus NAc are preferentially activated by aversion- versus reward-predictive cues, and activation of BLA-to-CeA versus BLA-to-NAc promotes aversive versus appetitive behaviors (Kim et al., 2017; Beyeler et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activation of BLA-to-CeA versus BLA-to-NAc promotes aversive versus appetitive behaviors.
source: BLA neurons that project to the CeA versus NAc are preferentially activated by aversion- versus reward-predictive cues, and activation of BLA-to-CeA versus BLA-to-NAc promotes aversive versus appetitive behaviors (Kim et al., 2017; Beyeler et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rspo2 BLA neurons projecting to the CeA versus NAc are largely nonoverlapping, mediating distinct behavioral responses.
source: We speculate that Rspo2 BLA neurons projecting to the CeA versus NAc are largely nonoverlapping, mediating distinct behavioral responses.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the projection patterns and behavioral correlates.

claim: Mice establish instrumental responding for self-stimulation of the BLA-to-NAc projection as a whole.
source: Without differentiating Rspo2- or Ppp1r1b-to-NAc subprojections, previous studies show that mice establish instrumental responding for self-stimulation of the BLA-to-NAc projection as a whole (Stuber et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Activation of each of the BLA-to-NAc subprojections may function as an unconditioned reinforcer to drive the instrumental responding.
source: Taken together with our current results, activation of each of the BLA-to-NAc subprojections may function as an unconditioned reinforcer to drive the instrumental responding.
evidence: This is inferred from the ICSS data and previous literature.

claim: Low-frequency (i.e., 5 or 10 Hz over ~5 s) stimulations of BLA neurons do not establish ICSS.
source: Specifically, low-frequency (i.e., 5 or 10 Hz over ~5 s) stimulations of BLA neurons do not establish ICSS (Servonnet et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: High-frequency stimulations of presynaptic terminals can strongly activate the soma of BLA neurons through potential backpropagation.
source: Through potential backpropagation, such high-frequency stimulations of presynaptic terminals can strongly activate the soma of BLA neurons, which, in turn, activate other BLA-projected brain regions that are involved in US-mediated reinforcement.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on known properties of neuronal backpropagation.

claim: Direct or indirect BLA projections innervate neurons in the ventral tegmental area, prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and lateral hypothalamus, all implicated in behavioral reinforcement.
source: Indeed, direct or indirect BLA projections are detected to innervate neurons in the ventral tegmental area, prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and lateral hypothalamus, all implicated in behavioral reinforcement (Janak and Tye, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In addition to BLA-to-NAc subprojections, other divergent projections from the BLA may also be activated to substantiate the US-mediated reinforcement during ICSS training.
source: Thus, in addition to BLA-to-NAc subprojections, other divergent projections from the BLA may also be activated to substantiate the US-mediated reinforcement during ICSS training.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the potential for backpropagation and known BLA projection patterns.

claim: The BLA-to-NAc projection is essential for cue-conditioned incentive processing.
source: It has long been known that the BLA-to-NAc projection is essential for cue-conditioned incentive processing (Robinson and Berridge, 1993; Chang et al., 2012; Keefer et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Compared to the anterior BLA, the posterior BLA is more enriched in Ppp1r1b neurons and send projections to both the NAc shell and core.
source: Specifically, compared to the anterior BLA, the posterior BLA is more enriched in Ppp1r1b neurons and send projections to both the NAc shell and core (Kim et al., 2016; Kita and Kitai, 1990; Russchen and Price, 1984; Brog et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Disconnecting the BLA and NAc shell impairs outcome-specific Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer and the maintenance of cue-conditioned responding in the absence of reward.
source: Disconnecting the BLA and NAc shell impairs outcome-specific Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer and the maintenance of cue-conditioned responding in the absence of reward (Simmons and Neill, 2009; Shiflett and Balleine, 2010; Corbit and Balleine, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Among the NAc shell and core projections, the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc shell branch may be particularly important for cue-conditioned reinforcement.
source: Thus, among the NAc sell and core projections, the Ppp1r1b-to-NAc shell branch may be particularly important for cue-conditioned reinforcement.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the anatomical distribution and previous functional studies.

claim: Lesion of the BLA does not prevent the acquisition of instrumental responding to rewards.
source: This is in line with the findings that lesion of the BLA does not prevent the acquisition of instrumental responding to rewards (Keefer et al., 2021; Balleine et al., 2003; Holland and Gallagher, 2003; Wassum and Izquierdo, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The BLA is not essential for first-order cue conditioning under many experimental conditions.
source: Indeed, the BLA is also not essential for first-order cue conditioning under many experimental conditions (Hatfield et al., 1996; Blundell et al., 2001; Parkinson et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activation of the Ppp1r1b subprojection is sufficient to establish cue conditioning.
source: Albeit nonessential, our ICSS results suggest that activation of the Ppp1r1b subprojection is sufficient to establish cue conditioning (Figure 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the cue-induced ICSS seeking data shown in Figure 2.

claim: BLA inputs to the NAc are likely among several parallel and potentially redundant circuits that collectively contribute to cue conditioning during motivated behaviors.
source: Thus, BLA inputs to the NAc are likely among several parallel and potentially redundant circuits that collectively contribute to cue conditioning during motivated behaviors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the non-essential but sufficient role of BLA inputs.

claim: The Ppp1r1b subprojection preferentially regulates the execution of cue-reinforced cocaine seeking rather than the acquisition.
source: Thus, instead of the acquisition (Figure 3), the Ppp1r1b subprojection preferentially regulates the execution of cue-reinforced cocaine seeking.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects on cocaine SA acquisition versus cue-induced seeking.

claim: Disconnection and chemo- or optogenetic inhibition of BLA-to-NAc projection compromise the performance of cue-controlled reward seeking.
source: This is consistent with the previous results that disconnection and chemo- or optogenetic inhibition of BLA-to-NAc projection compromise the performance of cue-controlled reward seeking (Ambroggi et al., 2008; Stuber et al., 2011; Di Ciano and Everitt, 2004), including cue-induced cocaine seeking under a second-order schedule of reinforcement (Puaud et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The BLA-to-NAc projection is one of the primary circuit targets for drug experience, with the resulting adaptive changes promoting drug seeking.
source: Emerging evidence suggests that the BLA-to-NAc projection is one of the primary circuit targets for drug experience, with the resulting adaptive changes promoting drug seeking.
evidence: This is a general statement based on emerging evidence in the field.

claim: After withdrawal from cue-conditioned cocaine SA, the overall strength of randomly sampled BLA-to-NAc synapses is increased.
source: For example, after withdrawal from cue-conditioned cocaine SA, the overall strength of randomly sampled BLA-to-NAc synapses is increased, and reversing this cocaine-induced strengthening decreases cue-induced cocaine seeking (Zinsmaier et al., 2022; Pascoli et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Reversing cocaine-induced strengthening of BLA-to-NAc synapses decreases cue-induced cocaine seeking.
source: For example, after withdrawal from cue-conditioned cocaine SA, the overall strength of randomly sampled BLA-to-NAc synapses is increased, and reversing this cocaine-induced strengthening decreases cue-induced cocaine seeking (Zinsmaier et al., 2022; Pascoli et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The behavioral reversal of cue-induced cocaine seeking is observed upon manipulation of BLA inputs to the NAc shell.
source: In these studies, the behavioral reversal is observed upon manipulation of BLA inputs to the NAc shell.
evidence: This is a statement about previous studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: The Ppp1r1b subprojection is the primary bearer of cocaine-induced adaptations that promote cue-induced cocaine seeking.
source: Among the heterogenous BLA-to-NAc projections, we speculate that the Ppp1r1b subprojection is the primary bearer of cocaine-induced adaptations that promote cue-induced cocaine seeking.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the current findings and previous literature.

claim: Previous studies demonstrate opposite roles of Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons in appetitive versus aversive reinforcement by manipulating somatic activities or projections to the CeA.
source: By manipulating somatic activities or projections to the CeA, previous studies demonstrate opposite roles of Rspo2 and Ppp1r1b BLA neurons in appetitive versus aversive reinforcement (Kim et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The established behavioral correlates of Rspo2 BLA neurons may be mediated by the projections of Rspo2 BLA to other brain regions.
source: As such, a lack of behavioral effects in our results may suggest that the established behavioral correlates of Rspo2 BLA neurons are mediated by the projections of Rspo2 BLA to other brain regions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the lack of effect of Rspo2-to-NAc manipulation on cue-induced cocaine seeking.

claim: Rspo2-Cre and Cartpt-Cre mice were obtained from the Tonegawa lab.
source: Both Rspo2-Cre and Cartpt-Cre mice with the C57BL/6J background were obtained from the Tonegawa lab (Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the source of the mouse lines used in the study.

claim: The D1-tdTomato mouse line was purchased from the Jackson Lab.
source: The D1-tdTomato mouse line (strain number 016204) was purchased from the Jackson Lab (Bar Harbor, ME, USA) and bred in house.
evidence: This is a statement about the source of the mouse line used in the study.

claim: Male mice were used in all experiments.
source: Male mice were used in all experiments.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design.

claim: Ppp1r1b is also known as DARPP-32.
source: These BLA neurons are genetically separable into two populations, R-spondin2-positive (Rspo2) magnocellular neurons and protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B-positive (Ppp1r1b, also known as DARPP-32) parvocellular neurons (Kim et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established nomenclature in neuroscience.

claim: Ppp1r1b BLA neurons can be genetically targeted through cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript protein (Cartpt)-Cre mice.
source: Ppp1r1b BLA neurons can be genetically targeted through cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript protein (Cartpt)-Cre mice (Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.
